description_full: Reckitt Benckiser Group plc manufactures and sells health, hygiene, and nutrition products in the United Kingdom and internationally. The company offers germ protection under Dettol name; intimate wellness under Durex and KY brand names; over the counter under the Biofreeze, Gaviscon, Mucinex, Nurofen, Delsym, Cepacol, and Strepsils names. It also provides personal care products under Clearasil and Veet brand names; vitamins, minerals, and supplements under MegaRed, Airborne, Digestive-Advantage, Movefree, and neuriva names; stain removal under Vanish brand name; and disinfectant products under the Finish, Harpic, and Lysol brands. In addition, the company offers nutritious complementary foods and milk formulas for infant and young children under the Enfamil and Nutramigen brands. Reckitt Benckiser Group plc was founded in 1819 and is headquartered in Slough, the United Kingdom.

CEO compensation is 11× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity). R&D investment of 2% of revenue (limited) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc. is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $47.4B market cap on $19.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 16% against a 6% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 60% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $2.2B in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.72× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.1×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
